output.summary: KEP-3705 extends kubelet --node-ip so that clusters using an external cloud provider can specify dual-stack node IPs (including IPv4/IPv6 family selectors), and defines how kubelet passes that intent to the cloud provider via the provided-node-ip annotation. Status is implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: Kubelet accepted dual-stack --node-ip only without a cloud provider, so cloud-provider clusters could not override both node IPs. The KEP limits the change to --node-ip values that older kubelets would have rejected, leaving default behavior unchanged. The annotation rename was dropped from scope and the feature was moved to a staged rollout. Testing gaps for dual-stack cloud jobs were discussed during review.

alternatives.option: Pass 0.0.0.0 and :: through to the cloud provider and let them mean 'any IP of that family'
alternatives.why_not: For compatibility reasons the existing behavior of --cloud-provider external --node-ip :: cannot change, so the KEP adds new IPv4/IPv6 syntax instead.

alternatives.option: Rename the alpha.kubernetes.io/provided-node-ip annotation as part of this KEP
alternatives.why_not: The Non-Goals say renaming the annotation is no longer planned as part of this feature.

alternatives.option: Replace --node-ip with a new plural --node-ips flag now
alternatives.why_not: The KEP says a new --node-ips flag would need a larger redesign and 'will have to wait for another KEP'.

alternatives.option: Support nodes whose cloud does not know the requested node IP
alternatives.why_not: It is a non-goal: the KEP does not add the ability to use node IPs not already known to the cloud provider.

evidence.quote: Allow administrators of clusters using external cloud providers to override both node IPs on a node in a dual-stack cluster.
Changing the node-IP-selection behavior in any currently-existing Kubernetes cluster. This means that the default behavior when `--node-ip` is not specified will remain the same
Renaming `alpha.kubernetes.io/provided-node-ip` annotation. This was also proposed in the original version of this KEP, but is no longer planned as part of this feature.
Yes, it seems so. Status is `implemented`: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/96793299c9cdbdf9033a99592602c3ea7d14a0b3/keps/sig-network/3705-cloud-node-ips/kep.yaml#L9
We can't test the behavior of dual-stack `--node-ip` in clouds unless we have dual-stack e2e jobs in those clouds.
